messages:
amanda: 🚨 Heads-up — seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and timeouts from hosted inference gateway starting ~10:23 UTC. Support reports multiple customers with `502`/`504`. Example request_id: req_0a1b2c3d. Gateway latency tail went from ~200ms -> 800ms then timeouts. Attaching quick logs below, will start a warroom if this persists.

devon: Any change windows or config deploys around that time?

amanda: Not from infra side that I know of. Priya, did any routing changes land last night?

priya: I pushed a routing weight tweak around 02:00 UTC yesterday to shift traffic to gpt-lite variants for cost testing. Nothing major but can revert if you think it's related.

ryan: I'm seeing auth-proxy returning intermittent `500` when validating tokens for a subset of requests — stacktrace points to a downstream cache miss followed by a DB timeout. Correlating with the request_ids now.

infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway cpu_high r-gw-prod-3 = 95% (6m), autoscaler added 2 nodes.

sre-oncall: Mitigations we can do now: 1) enable circuit-breaker for heavy routes to 0.5, 2) force-fallback to stable model variant for high latency clients, 3) increase gateway concurrency limit temporarily. I'll apply 1 & 2 now.

priya: Rolling back routing weight to previous commit. Command:```bash
# rollback routing weights
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://infra.internal/api/v1/routing/revert -d '{"to":"v341"}'
```Applying now.

deploy-bot: rollback activated: routing-config v342 -> v341. Rolling restart on gw-pool-1 started (3 hosts).

ryan: Added extra logging to auth-proxy and extended DB client timeout to 3s as a stopgap. Will monitor.

amanda: Support: affected customers flagged: acme-inc, study-app, chatly. Sending status update and customer-facing message. Suggest we offer token of free credits while we investigate.

devon: Early hypothesis: routing tweak increased load on a smaller backend pool that exercises a less-optimized auth path. Auth cache misses + DB timeout => backend thrash => gateway tail latency and 5xx. Need repro.

ryan: Repro steps I used locally (small script):```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN_TYPE_X" -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' 
    -m 2 
    https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate || echo "failed $i"
done
```
This reproduces intermittent 502s under the auth-proxy path when cache is cold.

priya: Confirmed: after revert latency dropped and error-rate fell ~70% in the last 8m. We still saw a small number of errors tied to auth-proxy DB timeouts.

sre-oncall: Current status: traffic reverted, circuit-breaker in place, autoscaler stabilized the pool. Monitoring for 30m before declaring resolved.

amanda: Action items (assign):
- priya: write a postmortem draft including exact routing delta + rollforward/rollback timeline. (assign to @priya)
- ryan: add more robust caching and retry logic in auth-proxy + increase observability spans for token validation path. (assign to @ryan)
- devon: create a canary test that simulates cold auth-caches + backend weight shifts to catch this in CI. (assign to @devon)
- amanda: coordinate customer comms and update status page. (assign to @amanda)
- sre-oncall: validate autoscaler thresholds and make recommendations to avoid thrash. (assign to @sre-oncall)

devon: Target for initial postmortem draft: EOD today. Add a follow-up meeting tomorrow to finalize.

deploy-bot: healthcheck: gw-pool-1 OK, gw-pool-2 OK, auth-proxy instances healthy.

infra-bot: METRICS: 5xx-rate down from 18% -> 3% in last 10m. CPU back to 45% on r-gw-prod-3.

amanda: Great, closing this warroom for now. We'll continue monitoring; reopen if errors climb again. Postmortem thread: /channels/postmortems (will link the artifact once priya starts draft). Thanks all :thumbsup:
